title: The Cave
full_review:
Late in "The Cave" (Screen Gems), one of the ill-fated cave explorers intuits that the ravenous creatures terrorizing them aren't just looking for a quick bite: "They want to get out." Those trapped in the audience may find themselves craving an exit as well.

The directorial debut of Bruce Hunt, this schlocky horror action film centers around a team (headed by Cole Hauser and Eddie Cibrian) leading a scientific expedition through a labyrinthine system of caverns recently discovered deep below a 13th-century abbey in a remote mountain region of Romania.

An explosion seals the crew's (including Piper Perabo) escape. As if being marooned miles beneath the surface -- with limited supplies -- isn't bad enough, they soon find themselves falling prey to an unknown subterranean species of giant batlike carnivores.

Not without occasional jolts and a clever "Body Snatchers" twist, "The Cave" echoes the claustrophobic creepiness of "Alien" and, in the hands of a more accomplished director, could have been a fun and -- much scarier -- B-movie. But Hunt is no Ridley Scott, and his inexperience shows. It doesn't help his cause that he had to work with a hackneyed script -- rife with laughable dialogue -- that, shall we say, caves in under the weight of its illogic.

It is essential in these types of movies that you care about the characters, but how is that possible when they merely serve -- or are served up -- as hors d'oeuvres to be picked off at regular intervals?

As it is, this "Cave" is a formulaic and forgettable group-peril flick not worth exploring.

This film contains recurring monster menace and bloody gore, as well as scattered crude language and profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
